title: Quitting a background app that doesn't implement org.freedesktop.Application.quit sends SIGKILL, which can be destructive. Consider SIGTERM instead
line: Quitting a Flatpak background app from the system tray now asks it to close normally, so apps like Chrome keep their session instead of being killed.
explanation: When a background app doesn't implement org.freedesktop.Application.quit (Chrome doesn't), the tray's Quit went straight to 'flatpak kill', which sends SIGKILL to the sandbox, so the app can't save anything and Chrome reports a crash. The process flatpak reports for an instance (child-pid) is bubblewrap's init, which ignores SIGTERM, so the app to signal is its child that has pid 2 inside the sandbox. Now the tray asks 'flatpak ps' for each instance's sandbox, sends SIGTERM to that process, and only runs 'flatpak kill' if it is still running 10 seconds later (or right away if the process can't be found).

commits.message:
applets/systemtray: Send SIGTERM to background apps before killing them

Apps without org.freedesktop.Application.quit were SIGKILLed right away
by flatpak kill, so Chrome lost its session. Now the app's main process
gets SIGTERM first and flatpak kill only runs if it's alive 10 s later.

BUG: 524863

media.caption: Master: Quit on a sandboxed background app that saves its session on SIGTERM; plasmashell runs flatpak kill and the app dies without its SIGTERM handler running
With the fix: the same Quit sends SIGTERM to the app, which saves and exits cleanly; flatpak kill is never run

review.text: Reasonable and contained: it sends SIGTERM to the app's main process (the pid-2 child of bubblewrap's init, found via the public 'flatpak ps' child-pid column and /proc) and falls back to 'flatpak kill' after 10 s or when the process can't be found, so Quit still always quits and no strings are added. It relies on flatpak's bwrap layout (app at NSpid 2), which is stable in practice. The checks before killing guard against PID reuse. It was only tested with a bwrap stand-in, not a real Flatpak, so a check with real Chrome before merging would help.
